messages.subject: Rattle 4.0.5 on R 3.2.3 working on RHEL 5
messages.subject_clean: Rattle 4.0.5 on R 3.2.3 working on RHEL 5
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have installed Rattle 4.0.5 along with R 3.2.3 on Red hat enterprise linux 5.4 /

Here is my Rattleinfo():

Rattle: version 4.0.5 CRAN 4.1.0
R: version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)

Sysname: Linux
Release: 2.6.18-164.el5
Version: #1 SMP Tue Aug 18 15:51:48 EDT 2009

Installed Dependencies
cluster: version 2.0.3
foreign: version 0.8-66
Matrix: version 1.2-3
nnet: version 7.3-11 upgrade available 7.3-12
rpart: version 4.1-10
stringr: version 1.0.0
survival: version 2.38-3

That was 8 packages.

When  i run rattle  then i get the following error

rattle()
Error in as.GType(type) : Cannot convert RGtkBuilder to GType.

I have gtk2 and gtk2-devel installed.

Upgrading RHEL 5.4 to  6 is not an option as this is a Linux cluster.

Any way this problem can be solved ?

messages.body_plain:
According to http://rattle.togaware.com/rattle-install-troubleshooting.html the likely problem is the use of an old version of gtk2. You may need to find an updated version of gtk2 that is compiled for RHEL 5.4

Regards,
Graham Williams

messages.subject: Error trying to run a RandomForest
messages.subject_clean: Error trying to run a RandomForest
messages.body_plain:
Can anyone help me?  I am having the following error message when I try to run a randomForest on a small data set.  I am getting the following error message

An error occured in the call to 'randomForest::randomForest'. The error message was:

Error in na.roughfix.data.frame(structure(list(`as.factor(mod7_5class)` = structure(c(3L,  :
  na.roughfix only works for numeric or factor

If this is a bug please contact sup...@togaware.com.

Please supply the output of rattleInfo() and the steps required to replicate the problem.

Rattle 4.1.0

My target variable has 5 values and it is indicated as categoric on the data tab.  Tree works fine!

Thanks for any assistance!

Tom

messages.body_plain:
Good Morning, I get this too.

As I understand it, there is a variable in your dataset, where its class is not a factor, and it needs to be.

If the variable and do something like   dataset$variablename <- as.factor(ldataset$variablename)

That should fix it up, as I understand it. But I am not the best r coder, so I might be wrong also.

Hope it helps

Regards

tony

messages.subject: Re: latticist is not supported in Rattle 4.1.0 ?
messages.subject_clean: latticist is not supported in Rattle 4.1.0 ?
messages.body_plain:
The latticist package is no longer supported by its author on CRAN and hence can not be included in Rattle.

Regards,
Graham Williams
